title: Cover letters
examples: How do I make sure my cover letter sounds professional enough?
What is the best way to tailor a cover letter for a specific job?
Should I write a different cover letter for every job I apply to?

explain.say: A cover letter introduces you to the hiring manager.

items: It explains your interest in the role.
It should be formal and polite.

explain.say: Tailoring means changing your letter for each job.
The structure must include a clear opening paragraph.
The middle body paragraphs provide evidence of your skills.

items: Paragraph 3: Why you fit the company

explain.say: The final paragraph must include a clear call to action.
In real life, you must tailor your letter to the company's mission.

faq.q: How long should a cover letter be?
faq.a: It should ideally fit onto one page. Keep it concise and impactful.
asks: Can I write more than one page?
What is the ideal length for this letter?

faq.q: What if I don't know the hiring manager's name?
faq.a: Use a title like 'Hiring Team' or 'Recruiting Manager'. Avoid using 'To Whom It May Concern'.
asks: Who should I address it to?
What is a safe greeting if I don't know the name?

faq.a: No, it means adapting your core stories and keywords to match the job description's needs.
asks: Do I need to change every sentence?

faq.q: Should I use fancy fonts or colors?
faq.a: Stick to professional, readable fonts like Times New Roman or Arial. Black ink is always best.
asks: What font style is considered professional?

faq.q: What is the purpose of the opening sentence?
faq.a: It must immediately grab attention and state why you are writing. Do not start with pleasantries.
asks: What should the first sentence achieve?

facts: A cover letter should never repeat everything from your resume.
Always address the letter to a specific person if possible.
The tone must be professional, confident, and enthusiastic.
A strong closing asks for the next step, like an interview.

quiz.say: Which action shows the best tailoring?

options.show: Writing a letter about your general career goals.
options.say: Writing a letter about your general career goals.

options.show: Using highly technical jargon from your field.
options.say: Using highly technical jargon from your field.

options.show: Highlighting experience in data analysis for a finance role.
options.say: Highlighting experience in data analysis for a finance role.

options.show: Listing all your skills from your university coursework.
options.say: Listing all your skills from your university coursework.

quiz.why: This directly connects your past work to the specific needs of the finance job.

wrong.0: This is too vague; the letter must focus on the advertised position.
wrong.1: This can confuse the reader if they are not experts in that specific jargon.
wrong.3: This is too general and does not prove relevance to the job.

quiz.say: What is the main purpose of the body paragraphs?

options.show: Providing specific examples that prove you have the required skills.
options.say: Providing specific examples that prove you have the required skills.

options.show: Simply restating the job description requirements.
options.say: Simply restating the job description requirements.

options.show: Writing about unrelated achievements to impress the reader.
options.say: Writing about unrelated achievements to impress the reader.

options.show: Apologizing for any gaps in your employment history.
options.say: Apologizing for any gaps in your employment history.

quiz.why: The body is where you use evidence to back up the claims made in the job description.

wrong.1: This shows you read it, but it does not show you have the skills.
wrong.2: Every sentence must relate back to why you want this specific job.
wrong.3: The letter should be positive and forward-looking, not defensive.

quiz.say: If the job description emphasizes teamwork, what should you focus on?

options.show: A brief story about successfully working with a diverse team.
options.say: A brief story about successfully working with a diverse team.

options.show: Describing your individual awards and accomplishments.
options.say: Describing your individual awards and accomplishments.

options.show: Mentioning your ability to work long hours.
options.say: Mentioning your ability to work long hours.

options.show: Listing software programs you know how to use.
options.say: Listing software programs you know how to use.

quiz.why: This directly addresses the key requirement of teamwork using a concrete example.

wrong.1: While good, this ignores the specific requirement for teamwork mentioned.
wrong.2: This is a general work ethic point, not specific to teamwork skills.
wrong.3: Software skills are useful, but they do not prove collaborative ability.
